name: @gtkx/mcp

tools.name: gtkx_list_apps
tools.description: List connected GTKX applications and their open windows. An app whose windows cannot be read, such as one an error stopped under `gtkx dev`, has `error` in place of `windows`. Returns the current snapshot unless waitForApps is true; only the first seconds of a new server session wait for running apps to reconnect.

waitForApps.description: If true, wait for at least one app to register before returning. Useful when app is still starting.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds when waitForApps is true (default: 10000)

tools.name: gtkx_get_widget_tree
tools.description: Get the widget hierarchy for a connected GTKX app. Returns a tree of widgets with their IDs, types, roles, and properties. For large apps, pass `maxDepth` for a shallow overview and/or `rootId` to render just one subtree instead of the whole (possibly truncated) tree.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

rootId.description: Render only the subtree rooted at this widget ID (from a prior tree or query). Omit for the whole app.

maxDepth.description: Limit how many levels deep to render, and 0 for the root widget on its own; deeper descendants are summarized with a count. Combine with rootId to drill in without dumping the whole tree.

tools.name: gtkx_query_widgets
tools.description: Find widgets by role, text, name, or label. Returns each match with its ID and the same fixed summary `gtkx_get_widget_props` returns, with no descendants: a match that has children carries `hiddenChildren`, the count of its direct children left out. Read a match's subtree with `gtkx_get_widget_props` or `gtkx_get_widget_tree`.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

by.description: What to compare value with: "role" the accessible role (such as "button" or "checkbox"), "text" the text the widget renders, "labelText" its label, and "name" the widget name (the GType name when none was set), the accessible name, the label and the rendered text.

value.description: Value to search for, matched whole unless options.exact is false

name.description: With by:"role", the accessible name the widget must also have.

exact.description: When true (the default), the value and name must match whole and case-sensitively; when false, they match case-insensitively as substrings.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to keep retrying while nothing matches (default: 1000).

tools.name: gtkx_get_widget_props
tools.description: Read a widget's type, accessible role, accessible name, text, sensitivity, visibility, CSS classes, and descendants. Defaults to 8 levels; `maxDepth` changes the depth. Results contain at most 30 widgets, in breadth-first order. `hiddenChildren` counts omitted direct children; query that widget's ID to expand it. Use `gtkx_get_widget_tree` for an overview. Requested GObject `properties` appear first, keyed by canonical kebab-case name with `{type, value}`. Enum/flags values use GType value names, 64-bit integers use decimal strings, boxed values such as `GdkRGBA` use their string form, and objects use their GType name plus `widgetId` for widgets. Unknown properties fail; values that cannot be converted include a `note`.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

widgetId.description: Widget ID obtained from `gtkx_get_widget_tree`, `gtkx_query_widgets`, or `gtkx_get_widget_props`. IDs are scoped to a single app. An ID stays valid for as long as its widget is mounted and stops resolving once the widget is unmounted.

properties.description: GObject property names to read as well, in kebab-case or camelCase ("current-breakpoint" or "currentBreakpoint"). Omit for the summary alone.

maxDepth.description: How many levels of descendants to include: 8 by default, and 0 for the widget on its own. At most 30 widgets come back whatever the depth, and any widget whose own direct children were left out carries a `hiddenChildren` count.

tools.name: gtkx_take_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of a window. Returns base64-encoded PNG image data, and optionally writes the PNG to `path` on the app's machine. You can't target widgets from a screenshot; use `gtkx_get_widget_tree` to find widget IDs for interaction. A screenshot taken right after an interaction can catch an animation midway; take another once it finishes.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

windowId.description: Window ID to capture. If not specified, captures the first window.

path.description: Absolute path to write the PNG to on the app's machine. If set, the screenshot is saved there in addition to being returned.

returnImage.description: Return the PNG as image content (default: true). Set false with `path` to save the image and return only its file location.

tools.name: gtkx_click
tools.description: Click a widget through userEvent.click. Works with buttons, checkboxes, switches, list and grid rows, tree expanders, and column headers: a row is selected, an expander toggles its row's expansion, and a header sorts its column. A widget a pointer cannot reach, such as one behind an open dialog, is refused with an error naming what blocks it. A widget inside one that cannot receive pointer input, such as a tab overview title, is refused with the widget ID of the ancestor a pointer lands on instead; click that ID. The result says when nothing on the widget or its ancestors handled the click, as with GTK's own widgets such as a color chooser's swatches, which need a real pointer; press {Space} or {Enter} on them with `gtkx_press_keys` instead.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

widgetId.description: Widget ID obtained from `gtkx_get_widget_tree`, `gtkx_query_widgets`, or `gtkx_get_widget_props`. IDs are scoped to a single app. An ID stays valid for as long as its widget is mounted and stops resolving once the widget is unmounted.

tools.name: gtkx_type
tools.description: Type text into an editable widget like Entry or TextView. A newline is typed as text and does not submit; use `gtkx_press_keys` with {Enter} to activate an entry. Typing replaces text that is already selected, as it does for a user: GTK selects an entry's whole text when focus moves into it, such as when a dialog opens on it. Pass `clear` with the full text to set a value. A widget behind an open dialog is refused with an error naming the dialog, and typing while `gtkx_press_keys` holds a modifier is refused with an error naming it.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

widgetId.description: Widget ID obtained from `gtkx_get_widget_tree`, `gtkx_query_widgets`, or `gtkx_get_widget_props`. IDs are scoped to a single app. An ID stays valid for as long as its widget is mounted and stops resolving once the widget is unmounted.

tools.name: gtkx_press_keys
tools.description: Press keys through userEvent.keyboard, as a user would on the keyboard: {Enter} activates an entry and the dialog's default response, {Escape} closes a dialog or popover, and shortcuts such as `{Control>}s{/Control}` run the actions bound to them. Keys reach the widget's own key bindings first, such as arrows in a list or slider; otherwise {Tab}, `{Shift>}{Tab}{/Shift}` and arrows move focus between widgets. {Space} or {Enter} also selects or activates GTK's own widgets, such as a color chooser's swatches. The result names the keys that nothing on the widget or its ancestors handled. A modifier pressed with `{Control>}` stays held across calls until released with `{/Control}`, and the result names the modifiers left held. Use `gtkx_type` to enter text.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

widgetId.description: Widget ID obtained from `gtkx_get_widget_tree`, `gtkx_query_widgets`, or `gtkx_get_widget_props`. IDs are scoped to a single app. An ID stays valid for as long as its widget is mounted and stops resolving once the widget is unmounted. A widget that can take focus, or passes it to a child as a menu button does to its button, is focused first, as a user would before typing. One that cannot, such as the switch inside a switch row, leaves the window's focus where it is, and the result names its nearest ancestor that can take focus to press the keys on instead. Omit it to press the keys on the focused widget of the active window, or of the first window when none is active.

keys.description: Keys to press in order. A plain character presses that key. Name other keys in braces: {Enter}, {Escape}, {Tab}, {Backspace}, {Delete}, {Space}, {ArrowUp}, {ArrowDown}, {ArrowLeft}, {ArrowRight}, {Home}, {End}, {PageUp}, {PageDown} and {F1} to {F12}. Hold a modifier with {Control>}, {Shift>}, {Alt>} or {Meta>} and release it with {/Control} and so on, so Ctrl+S is `{Control>}s{/Control}`.

tools.name: gtkx_pointer
tools.description: Press a mouse button on a widget through userEvent.pointer, with one pointer token in `input`. `[MouseRight]` right-clicks: it reaches the click gestures on the widget and its ancestors that listen for the secondary button, such as a `GtkGestureClick` with `button={Gdk.BUTTON_SECONDARY}` that opens a context menu. `[MouseMiddle]` does the same for the middle button, and `[MouseLeft]` clicks like `gtkx_click`. Hold a button with `[MouseRight>]` and release it with `[/MouseRight]`. A widget behind an open dialog is refused with an error naming the dialog.

applicationId.description: Application ID to query. If not specified, uses the connected app from this server's project, or the first connected app when none is from it. `gtkx storybook` registers its explorer under the project's ID with a `.Storybook` suffix; the project's app is preferred over it, and while the project's app is reconnecting (when this server has just started, or after a `gtkx dev` restart) the tool waits for it instead of using the explorer. The tool waits briefly for the requested app to register.

appTimeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the requested app to register, or for the project's app to reconnect before falling back to another app (default: 10000).

widgetId.description: Widget ID obtained from `gtkx_get_widget_tree`, `gtkx_query_widgets`, or `gtkx_get_widget_props`. IDs are scoped to a single app. An ID stays valid for as long as its widget is mounted and stops resolving once the widget is unmounted.

input.description: One pointer token: [MouseLeft], [MouseRight] or [MouseMiddle] clicks that button, a trailing > presses and holds it ([MouseRight>]) and a leading / releases it ([/MouseRight]). click, down and up are the left button.

args.description: Arguments to pass to the signal

tools.name: gtkx_list_api
tools.description: List the project's generated bindings API (`@gtkx/gi` and `@gtkx/jsx`), including Adwaita, GTK4, and its declared GIR libraries. Without a namespace, returns every namespace with symbol counts; with a namespace, lists all of its symbols grouped by kind.

projectRoot.description: Directory of the GTKX project whose bindings to document, absolute or relative to the working directory. Any directory inside the project works; its `gtkx.config.ts` decides the documented libraries. Omit to use the project containing the working directory, falling back to a connected app's project.

namespace.description: Namespace to list (e.g. `Adw`, `Gtk`, `Gio`). Omit for an overview of all namespaces.

tools.name: gtkx_search_api
tools.description: Search the project's generated bindings API by name: classes, interfaces, records, enums, functions and other symbols, and the constructors, static methods, properties, signals, methods and record fields of classes, interfaces and records. Returns the best matches first, with namespace, kind and a one-line summary; a member's name is `Owner.member`. Read one with `gtkx_get_api_docs`.

projectRoot.description: Directory of the GTKX project whose bindings to document, absolute or relative to the working directory. Any directory inside the project works; its `gtkx.config.ts` decides the documented libraries. Omit to use the project containing the working directory, falling back to a connected app's project.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of a symbol or member name, e.g. `headerbar`, `replaceContentsAsync` or `close-request`. Include the owner, or the JSX element of a class, to list its members: `Gio.File.replace` or `GtkButton.icon`.

kind.description: Restrict matches to one symbol or member kind.

tools.name: gtkx_get_api_docs
tools.description: Get the reference page for one symbol of the project's generated bindings: JSX elements (props, signals, methods) or `@gtkx/gi` classes, interfaces, records, enums, callbacks, aliases, functions, and constants. A class page can run to hundreds of kilobytes; pass a member name such as `Gio.File.replaceContentsAsync` to get only that member's section.

projectRoot.description: Directory of the GTKX project whose bindings to document, absolute or relative to the working directory. Any directory inside the project works; its `gtkx.config.ts` decides the documented libraries. Omit to use the project containing the working directory, falling back to a connected app's project.

symbol.description: Qualified symbol name (`Adw.Toast`, `Gtk.Orientation`, `GLib.idleAdd`), JSX element name (`AdwToast`), bare symbol name when unambiguous (`Toast`), or a class, interface or record member named after its owner (`Gio.File.replaceContentsAsync`, `Gtk.Window.close-request`, `Gdk.RGBA.red`) or after the JSX element of its class (`AdwToast.title`), which returns only that member's section. A member a class inherits resolves to the ancestor or interface that documents it.

kind.description: Disambiguate when several kinds share the name, such as a class and its JSX element, or a signal and a method.

instructions:
The widget tools drive a GTKX app running under `gtkx dev`: they read its live widget tree, query it by accessible role and name, click and type, and capture screenshots. They wait briefly for a starting app, so start `gtkx dev` before or alongside a widget request. The reference tools answer from the bindings generated for a specific project, so they describe that project's GIR libraries rather than the GNOME platform in general; prefer them over recalled Adwaita or GTK knowledge, which is usually C, PyGObject or GJS and does not apply here.

Widget IDs are valid only while the widget is mounted. After a dialog closes, a list re-renders, or fast refresh patches a component, re-read the tree or re-run the query instead of reusing an ID.
